newsitem.title: MEXICO: Seven Mexican ports closed amid winds -gov't.
newsitem.headline: Seven Mexican ports closed amid winds -gov't.

text.p: Seven of Mexico's ports remained shut Wednesday as wind speeds exceeded 50 miles/80 km per hour, the Communications and Transport ministry said.

Six ports along the Gulf of Mexico were closed for the third consecutive day as of 1000 local time/1600 GMT, including the three main crude shipping ports of Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly.

Cayo Arcas in Campeche state ships an average 600,000 barrels per day (bpd), Pajaritos in Veracruz state exports about 400,000 bpd and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state ships 300,000 bpd, according to Platt's.
A cold front shuffling across the Gulf of Mexico and Yucatan peninsula sent winds and rain pounding Mexico's eastern coast.

Pemex's crude exports to the Far East were not halted by the closure of its terminal, Salina Cruz in Oaxaca state, according to the port capitan. The port remains shut to smaller boats because of high winds from a separate storm front, the ministry said.
Salina Cruz port capitan Idelfonso Carrillo Mora told Reuters the winds would not prevent crude oil loading and shipments, which leave the port about two to three times per month.
Weather reports indicate conditions could improve and the port could fully reopen within 24 hours, he added.
Ports closed earlier this week in the states of Yucatan and Tamaulipas have reopened, according to the ministry.
Other ports still closed include Veracruz and Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz, Frontera in Tabasco and Ciudad del Carmen and Campeche in Campeche. --Timna Tanners, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7903
